name: User Flow Diagram
description:
A user flow visualises the routes a person may take through a product or service to reach one or more goals. Unlike a simple task flow, it may include multiple entry points, decisions and alternative paths through the system.

User flows help designers examine how individual screens, states or touchpoints connect into a coherent experience.
whenToUse: Use user flows when designing navigation and interaction across multiple states or screens and when several routes through an experience need to be considered.
steps: Map major actions and system responses.
Include completion, exit and error states.
Review the flow for unnecessary complexity.
Compare it against research and scenarios.
Translate the flow into wireframes or prototypes.
Test whether actual users can navigate the intended paths.
lookOutFor: User flows can imply orderly behaviour that does not reflect real use.
Include returning users, interruptions and recovery where relevant.
Do not optimise every user toward the same route when people have legitimately different goals.

resources.citation: Garrett, J. J. (2011). *The Elements of User Experience*, 2nd ed. New Riders.
